events.title: Rock-ice avalanche, Lirung massif
events.detail: Seismic signal 02:52:10 UTC, M5.2 (USGS); ~100 million m³ of rock and ice

events.title: Gyirong Port destroyed
events.detail: CCTV captures destruction; ~20 km in ~7 min

events.title: Flood Forecasting Division informed
events.detail: Via Rasuwa District Administration and Betrawati station staff

events.title: Forecast: Galchhi and Mugling within hours
events.detail: Prithvi Highway and Mugling–Narayanghat road alerted

events.title: Phurke above danger; station and bridge lost
Devghat peaks at 6.57 m
events.detail: ~5,850 m³/s; 19.96 million m³ above normal flow

events.title: International Charter activated
events.detail: Requested by DHM; satellite mapping begins

story.title: The collapse
story.text: About 100 million m³ of rock and glacier ice breaks off the Lirung massif at ~5,200 m and drops ~1.2 km into the valley below. Seismometers around the world record it like an earthquake.

story.title: A debris flow forms
story.text: The falling mass turns into a debris flow: a fast slurry of mud, rock, ice and water that races down the narrow Lende Khola gorge at up to ~180 km/h.

story.title: The border crossing is hit
story.text: Seven minutes after the collapse it reaches the China–Nepal border and destroys Gyirong Port, a busy crossing for traders and pilgrims.

story.title: Almost no warning downstream
story.text: The flow enters Nepal through Timure and Syabrubesi. River gauges are destroyed one by one before they can raise an alarm.

story.title: Phones start to buzz
story.text: At 09:15 emergency SMS alerts reach 679,295 phones along the river. The front is slowing as the valley widens, but it is still a destructive surge.

story.title: Into the Trishuli
story.text: At Betrawati the surge enters the Trishuli. Hydropower projects, bridges and the road along the river are damaged or swept away.

story.title: A long, slower surge
story.text: Lower down the river is wider, so the flood spreads out and slows to roughly 25–30 km/h. Authorities have time to warn towns further downstream.

story.title: Malekhu
story.text: At 11:26 the river at Malekhu passes its warning level; by 11:43 the gauge and the Phurke bridge are swept away.

story.title: Past Mugling
story.text: By 13:00 the flood has passed Mugling. Riverside residents all the way to Devghat are told to move away from the banks.

story.title: Reaching the plains
story.text: At 15:20 it reaches Devghat and the Narayani. The river peaks at 6.57 m at 16:00, then falls. The flow carried debris, and the bodies of some victims, up to 250 km downstream.

story.title: What the map shows now
story.text: The shaded area is the flood extent mapped from satellites in the following days. Scrub the timeline or click a key event to revisit any moment.

after.title: Barrier lake warning (China MWR)

after.title: Lake 2 overflows
after.detail: Causes downstream rises; rescues briefly paused

rows: 14.2 km in ~350 s; mean 36 m/s at the border gorge
source.precursor: Sentinel-1 radar showed up to 40 cm of ground deformation at the source between 7 Jul and 24 Aug.
source.rain: No rain trigger: satellite rainfall over the catchment was 4.0 mm in the 24 h before failure (20th percentile) and 8.3 mm over 3 days (4th percentile).
source.conflicts: Published volume, magnitude and speed figures differ between studies; ranges are shown.
